title: Comprehensive and reproducible grading of the Updated Sydney System in gastric biopsies using artificial intelligence: multi-pathologist validation and a reader study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Comprehensive and reproducible grading of the Updated Sydney System in gastric biopsies using artificial intelligence: multi-pathologist validation and a reader study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · his70258-sec-0004-p4】To address these challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly been investigated in histopathology as a potential means of improving the reproducibility and efficiency of gastritis assessment. Early studies, however, mainly focused on narrow tasks, such as H. pylori detection or the separate grading of IM and atrophy. 12 More recent studies have extended this approach to two or three Sydney attributes. 13 , 14 However, in routine gastric biopsy interpretation, these five attributes frequently coexist and are assessed jointly. This creates two important gaps for clinical implementation. First, no previous framework has comprehensively evaluated all five USS attributes within a single model, particularly including H. pylori, which is central to the pathobiology of chronic gastritis. Second, prior studies have often relied on binary or reduced‐category predictions and were developed on relatively modest datasets annotated by a limited number of pathologists. Together, these limitations reduce clinical realism and generalizability, making implementation in routine pathology workflow more difficult.

【Introduction · his70258-sec-0004-p5】Here, we developed a unified, weakly supervised multi‐task learning framework that jointly predicts all five Sydney System attributes. We assembled a large‐scale cohort of over 50,000 histologically annotated whole‐slide images (WSIs)—to our knowledge, the largest gastritis dataset to date—capturing the full spectrum of gastric pathology. Further, using an expert‐adjudicated reference dataset, we evaluated whether this approach could support implementation in routine diagnostic workflow.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Comprehensive and reproducible grading of the Updated Sydney System in gastric biopsies using artificial intelligence: multi-pathologist validation and a reader study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Data Collection and Annotation · his70258-sec-0006-p2】Each H&E‐stained WSI from gastritis samples was interpreted according to the USS by a single reporting pathologist as part of routine clinical diagnosis. Cumulatively, the retrospective dataset comprised diagnostic labels contributed by multiple board‐certified pathologists. The USS defines five key histological attributes: mononuclear cell infiltration, neutrophil activity, glandular atrophy, IM and H. pylori density. The pathologist‐assigned labels and the AI inputs were derived from the same H&E‐stained WSIs. For H. pylori assessment in this dataset, ancillary special stains or immunohistochemistry (IHC) were not performed, reflecting routine high‐throughput diagnostic practice in which additional stains are not applied to every gastric biopsy. IM was graded according to the USS severity scale irrespective of histological subtype, and SydneyMTL was not trained to distinguish between these subtypes. Each attribute is graded on a four‐point ordinal scale (0 = Absent, 1 = Mild, 2 = Moderate, 3 = Marked). For mononuclear cell infiltration, grade 0 did not indicate complete absence of lamina propria lymphocytes or plasma cells, which may be present in normal gastric mucosa. Rather, it denoted the absence of chronic gastritis beyond the expected physiological inflammatory cell population, according to the USS visual analogue criteria. To ensure high clinical fidelity, we integrated ‘N/A’ (Not Applicable) as a distinct category for glandular atrophy, addressing cases where the absence of the muscularis mucosae precludes definitive grading. By incorporating the full spectrum of labels including ‘N/A’, SydneyMTL better reflects real‐world diagnostic variability and increases robustness to partially evaluable specimens. Unlike previous studies that exclude such cases, our framework explicitly learns these evaluation constraints, mimicking the high‐fidelity decision‐making process of pathologists who must identify non‐evaluable tissue in routine biopsy scenarios. An example of the structured USS report is provided in the Data S1.

【Model Evaluation Methods · his70258-sec-0008-p1】Model performance was evaluated using stratified fivefold cross‐validation on the retrospective dataset and independent testing on the Golden dataset. Because the USS is ordinal and semi‐quantitative, the primary performance measures were Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) and lenient accuracy. 16 , 17 For lenient accuracy, grade 0 required an exact match, whereas for grades 1–3, predictions within one adjacent category were considered correct provided that they did not cross the boundary between absent and pathological categories. To further examine whether the model preserved the ordinal structure of histological severity, we visualized slide‐level embeddings in a low‐dimensional space. Model interpretability was qualitatively assessed using attention heatmaps and patch‐level feature visualization.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Comprehensive and reproducible grading of the Updated Sydney System in gastric biopsies using artificial intelligence: multi-pathologist validation and a reader study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Principal Findings · his70258-sec-0019-p1】Accurate histological grading of gastric biopsies is essential for gastric cancer prevention and serves as the basis for risk stratification systems. However, the routine application of the USS is currently hindered by substantial interobserver variability and the labour intensive nature of assessing multiple histological attributes. In this study, we introduce SydneyMTL, the first unified framework capable of simultaneously performing four‐tier grading for all five Sydney System attributes. On the largest cohort of gastric biopsies to date (n = 50,765) and an adjudicated dataset, our model captures the comprehensive histological landscape of chronic gastritis. By automating the grading process with strict adherence to biological ordinality and expert consensus, this work represents a paradigm shift from subjective visual estimation to reproducible, quantitative computational pathology.

【Conclusions · abstract-3-1】AI can support more reproducible and efficient grading of Updated Sydney histological attributes in gastric biopsies. By combining multi-pathologist validation, consensus-based evaluation and explicit handling of non-assessable atrophy, SydneyMTL provides a clinically realistic decision-support approach for routine digital pathology.

By combining multi-pathologist validation, consensus-based evaluation and explicit handling of non-assessable atrophy, SydneyMTL provides a clinically realistic decision-support approach for routine digital pathology.
